package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// A doubly linked ring with a sentinel: every node reaches every other
// node and itself through next/prev, so the value graph is cyclic.
type node struct {
	next, prev *node
	ring       *ring
	Value      int
}

type ring struct {
	root node
	len  int
}

func newRing() *ring {
	r := &ring{}
	r.root.next = &r.root
	r.root.prev = &r.root
	return r
}

func (r *ring) insert(n, at *node) *node {
	n.prev = at
	n.next = at.next
	n.prev.next = n
	n.next.prev = n
	n.ring = r
	r.len++
	return n
}

func (r *ring) push(v int) *node {
	return r.insert(&node{Value: v}, r.root.prev)
}

func main() {
	r := newRing()
	a := r.push(1)
	b := r.push(2)
	// A cyclic pointee handed to the dependency must arrive finite.
	fmt.Println(a.Value, b.Value, a.next == b, b.prev == a, a.prev == &r.root)
	s := fmt.Sprintf("%d %t", r.len, a.next.next == &r.root)
	fmt.Println(s)
	// The same pointer handed twice in one call, and the sentinel itself.
	fmt.Println(fmt.Sprint(a == a, &r.root == r.root.next.prev))
	fmt.Printf("%d\n", b.next.Value+a.prev.next.Value)
	// The pointers themselves cross: %p is stable per pointer and distinct
	// between pointers; %v of the cyclic pointee prints Go's &{…} form with
	// nested pointers as addresses.
	fmt.Println(fmt.Sprintf("%p", a) == fmt.Sprintf("%p", a), fmt.Sprintf("%p", a) == fmt.Sprintf("%p", b))
	fmt.Println(fmt.Sprintf("%T", a), strings.HasPrefix(fmt.Sprint(a), "&{"), strings.Count(fmt.Sprint(r), "0x"))
	fmt.Println(fmt.Sprintf("%p", &r.root) == fmt.Sprintf("%p", a.prev))
}
